sentences: Credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises as the share of the credit limit in use goes up, with a strong effect overall.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency on file raises default risk in a step, with a moderate to strong effect.
Annual income is the other leading driver: higher income lowers default risk, with a moderate to strong effect.
Utilization matters more than delinquencies, and income matters more than the length of credit history.
Longer credit history is associated with lower default risk, but this effect is weak to moderate and ranks fourth to sixth in importance.
The effect of utilization does not depend on credit history length, so the two act largely separately.
Debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, and months at the current address have at most a moderate effect, while the number of recent credit inquiries and applicant age hardly matter.
Income and age do not interact in the model's predictions.
